Body Tracking is a motion capture technology used to collect a user's body position and movement information, and to convert it into reproducible pose data. Body Tracking enables users to perform actions such as running, kicking, stepping, lying down, and twisting in XR scenes, enriching the user's motion experience.
PICO's Body Tracking functionality must be used in conjunction with the [PICO Motion Tracker](/document/discover/xr-devices/). The PICO Motion Tracker can retrieve the user's body position and movement information. Body Tracking interfaces convert this information into pose data for multiple human body joints and assign it to entities in the virtual scene, enabling synchronized movement between the real human body and the virtual human body.
## Recommended content
It is recommended to read the "[Use DataProvider](/en_instructions-on-data-provider)" to learn how to use `DataProvider` to obtain tracking data, determine data availability, and determine the state of `DataProvider`.
## Limitations

* HMD tracking data can only be retrieved when the app is in Full Space state.
* You can only use the Body Tracking interfaces to obtain data after switching the tracking mode of the PICO Motion Tracker to Body Tracking.
* Body Tracking mode and Object Tracking mode are mutually exclusive. When Object Tracking mode is enabled, body tracking data cannot be output.

1. Retrieve a `BodyTrackingProvider` instance.
   ```Kotlin
   @Composable
   fun BodyTrackingSample() {
       val bodyTrackingProvider = remember { BodyTrackingProvider }
       // ...
   }
   ```

   The BodyTrackingProvider instance is a singleton, and the same instance is shared across the entire process.

2. Call `start()` to start `BodyTrackingProvider`, trigger calibration from the PICO Motion Tracker as needed, and call `stop()` when `BodyTrackingProvider` is no longer required.
   ```Kotlin
   @Composable
   fun BodyTrackingSample() {
       // ...
       DisposableEffect(bodyTrackingProvider) {
           bodyTrackingProvider.start(Builder().apply { needCalibration = true }.build())
       
           onDispose {
               bodyTrackingProvider.stop()
           }
       }
       // ...
   }
   ```

3. Use `dataFlow` to retrieve pose data for all body joints.
   You can choose different methods to retrieve data based on the specific scenario. For example, in a Composable function, you can use `dataFlow` to retrieve data; in ECS, you can use `latestData` to retrieve the latest data.

   ```Kotlin
   @Composable
   fun BodyTrackingSample() {
       // ...
       val bodyTrackingData by
           bodyTrackingProvider.dataFlow.collectAsState(
               initial = BodyTrackingData(BodyPose(emptyList()), 0L)
           )
       // ...
   }
   ```

4. Read pose data for all body joints, convert the data's coordinate system, and set the result to `Entity`.
   ```Kotlin
   @Composable
   fun BodyTrackingSample() {
       // ...
       SpatialView(
           update = { _, _ ->
               val jointEntities = rootEntity.getChildren()
               // In practice, you only need to find the entity corresponding to the relevant bone node
               bodyTrackingData.bodyPose.bodyJoints.forEachIndexed { index, bodyJoint ->
                   jointEntities[index].apply {
                       components[TransformComponent::class.java]?.apply {
                           val position = rootEntity.convertPositionFrom(bodyJoint.position, null)
                           val rotation = rootEntity.convertRotationFrom(bodyJoint.rotation, null)
                           setPosition(position)
                           setQuaternion(rotation)
                       }
                   }
               }
           }
       ) { content, _ ->
           // Initialize your entity
       }
       // ...
   }
   ```


### Complete code sample
The code below demonstrates how to obtain real-time tracking data for each body joint and update the pose of the corresponding skeletal entity in the scene one by one, thereby synchronizing human motion in the virtual scene.
```Kotlin
@Composable
fun BodyTrackingSample() {
    // Get a BodyTrackingProvider
    val bodyTrackingProvider = remember { BodyTrackingProvider }

    // Obtain real-time tracking data from dataFlow
    val bodyTrackingData by
        bodyTrackingProvider.dataFlow.collectAsState(
            initial = BodyTrackingData(BodyPose(emptyList()), 0L)
        )

    // Use tracking data within the Composable's lifecycle
    DisposableEffect(bodyTrackingProvider) {
        // Specify that calibration is required when starting tracking (needCalibration = true)
        bodyTrackingProvider.start(Builder().apply { needCalibration = true }.build())
        onDispose {
            bodyTrackingProvider.stop()
        }
    }
    
    // Create the root node in the scene
    val rootEntity: Entity = remember { Entity() }

    SpatialView(
        update = { _, _ ->
            val jointEntities = rootEntity.getChildren()


            // Iterate through each joint
            // In practice, you can update only the entity corresponding to the skeletal node as needed
            bodyTrackingData.bodyPose.bodyJoints.forEachIndexed { index, bodyJoint ->                
                jointEntities[index].apply {
                    components[TransformComponent::class.java]?.apply {
                        // Convert the tracking data to the coordinate system of the root node and set it to the corresponding joint node
                        val position = rootEntity.convertPositionFrom(bodyJoint.position, null)
                        val rotation = rootEntity.convertRotationFrom(bodyJoint.rotation, null)
                        setPosition(position)
                        setQuaternion(rotation)
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    ) { content, _ ->
        // Initialize your entity here, create each skeletal node, and attach them to rootEntity
    }
}
```

## Monitor body tracking calibration status
You can obtain the calibration status of the user's PICO Motion Tracker by adding a listener.
```Kotlin
val bodyTrackingStateListener = TrackingStateListener { 
    // Handle calibration status changes
     Log.i("BodyTracking", "Body tracking is now${it.status}")
}
bodyTrackingProvider.addTrackingStateListener(bodyTrackingStateListener)
```

The PICO Motion Tracker has three calibration states, which are:

* `INVALID`: Not yet calibrated
* `VALID`: Calibration complete; tracking data is accurate and available.
* `LIMITED`: Calibration is currently complete, but tracking performance is poor. For example, a PICO Motion Tracker is obstructed by clothing. Tracking data can be used, but may not be accurate.

## Body joint reference
The SDK supports tracking 24 body joints shown in the figure below.
![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/f474598fdfff49f69460b661178cb528~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image)
Below are the descriptions of related concepts:
| **Concept** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Coordinate  | Body joint data uses the same global coordinate system as the HMD data  |
| Root joint  | 0 (Pelvis)  |
| Parent/child joint  | Joints numbered from 1 to 23. Parent joints are located near the root joint, while the child joints are located near the end of the limbs.  |
| Bone  <br>   | A bone is a rigid part between two joints, and its pose is stored in the parent joint which is located near the root joint. For example, the pose of the bone of the lower leg is stored in the knee joint.  <br> More examples:  <br>  <br> * Joint 4 (LEFT_KNEE): It stores the location information of the left knee joint and the pose of the bone of the left lower leg.  <br> * Joint 7 (LEFT_ANKLE): It stores the location information of the left ankle joint and the pose of the bone of the left foot.  |
## API reference
The `BodyTrackingProvider` class provides Body Tracking-related interfaces. For more information, refer to the [API Reference](https://developer.picoxr.com/spatial-api/index.html).
